content:
Alyssa: heads-up — hitting progressive GPU memory growth in longctx paged-attention runs. After ~1.2M tokens we see KV cache page walk latency spike and intermittent stalls (short hangs of the serving thread).

Ben: which cluster/hw and workload? any recent changes to kernel selection or batching?

Alyssa: repro on canary h100 pool (mixed with a few rtx6000 nodes). workload is our longctx stress harness (sequences appended to reach ~30k per example), reuse_window=16384, dynamic batching enabled. This started after the kernel-selector change that prefers tiled kernels for >4k sequences.

Chris: can you paste the logs around the stall?

Alyssa: here's the condensed log (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-10T09:12:34Z] kvcache: allocate page slab id=0x3f2 size=2MB
[2026-03-10T09:12:40Z] kvcache: pagetable walk 12.4ms -> 58.9ms (steady growth)
[2026-03-10T09:12:40Z] kvcache: eviction start slab=0x3f2 refs=12 compacting
[2026-03-10T09:12:41Z] runtime: pagepointer jam detected; pending_walks=47 evict_inflight=3
[2026-03-10T09:12:41Z] gpu: kernel launch timeout (3000ms) on tiled-attn-kernel-2
```

Maya: "pagepointer jam" — we've seen similar naming before but not this pattern. Looks like pagetable walk latency grows and then compaction races with active KV refs.

Ben: two hypotheses: 1) tiled kernel changes memory access pattern that increases PT walk churn (more random reads across slab pages), 2) compaction/eviction code introduced a reorder that drops an active reference and later tries to free a page still referenced by a pending kernel. Either can yield the jam.

Rahul: I pulled perf counters from a repro run (short):
L2_TEX_REPLAY: 9.2e6
L2_ATOMIC: 1.1e6
NVLINK_IDLE: 23%
SM_STALL: 12% -> spikes to 65% during stall

Rahul: also saw a steady increase in the PT walk CPU time in our flamegraph; the hotspot is pager::walk_and_lock_range and then kvcache::try_compact_slab.

Chris: can you run with KV_PAGER_DEBUG=1 and KV_PAGER_ASSERT_REF? That will help catch double-free or premature free. Also try forcing kernel-selector to prefer linear kernels (env KERNEL_POLICY=linear) to rule out tiled kernel interaction.

Alyssa: running debug now. Quick notes: forcing linear kernels reduces the PT walk growth rate by ~60% and no stalls during a 10-run test. With tiled kernels the growth reproduces every run.

Ben: that strongly points to an access pattern change (tiled -> more scattered KV accesses) exposing a race in compaction. Possible: compaction moves metadata and updates PT pointers under the hood without a proper publish barrier.

Maya: can we add a quick mitigation? e.g., throttle concurrent compactions to 1 and add a short grace window before freeing pages referenced by recent kernels? If that stabilizes, we can ship the throttle while we root cause.

Alyssa: applied local patch to serialize compactions (single-threaded) and added a 250ms grace hold on page free. Re-ran stress: memory growth stops, stalls gone. Perf impact ~+3% latency p95 — acceptable for canary.

Chris: good temporary mitigation. For root cause: add diagnostic counters — per-page last_published_seq and pending_kernel_count. If pending_kernel_count > 0, compaction should skip (and emit a metric).

Rahul: logging from debug run showed a suspicious sequence: compaction observed refcount==0, scheduled free, but shortly after a delayed kernel touch increments a transient in-flight ref that leads to walk on a page being freed and resurrected, causing pointer bouncing and increased walk time. Sounds like an ordering issue with the eviction token vs kernel dispatch.

Ben: does the kernel dispatch path take the page snapshot before launching? If not, the window between snapshot and launch may be too wide. We may need to pin pages for the lifetime of a kernel (or use an epoch counter) so compaction defers until epoch advance.

Maya: action items:
- Ben: experiment with epoch-based pin (pin_on_dispatch, unpin_on_reclaim) and run the longctx stress across h100/rtx mix (due Fri).
- Chris: open minimal repro that reproduces with tiled kernels and attach nvprof trace (put tarball in s3).
- Rahul: add perf counter collection and flamegraph hook for pager hot paths.
- Alyssa: keep the serialized compaction + 250ms grace on canary for now.

DeployBot: canary patch deployed to h100-canary pool at 4109998890 by Alyssa :white_check_mark:

Alyssa: thanks. I'll follow up with the nvprof trace and the debug logs (uploader: s3://redwood-temp/kvcache/4109998887-debug.tar.gz).

Ben: if epoch pins fix it, we can implement a non-blocking pin that only prevents compaction (cheap). Otherwise we may need to revisit allocator metadata ordering.

Chris: I'll create the ticket and link the reproducer + traces. Marking blocker for next runtime patch.

Maya: nice triage everyone. Keep notes in the ticket. :thumbsup:
